newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products, except naphtha, track crude drop.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products, except naphtha, track crude drop.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products fell on Thursday to track crude oil's tumble to its weakest level since September, though naphtha held steady.
Gas oil weakness and lengthy supplies kept the pressure on jet fuel with a dearth of buying interest pegging the focus of trade on arbitrage options out of the region, traders said.
Libyan barrels were around high quotes +$1/+$2 with European material $2 higher cif Med, but traders expected these levels to continue to fall with benchmark quotes with few outlets seen.
Gas oil continued weak and avails were still growing.

Premiums for Russian gas oil cargoes remained under pressure from good avails and hefty avails out of the Baltic cramping trade to the North. Cargoes valued around cif high -1.50 cif Med after trade at the level on Wednesday for early Feb barrels.
High sulphur fuel oil was around a dollar weaker as crude fell and amid a still-lengthy supply situation.
An Alexandria tender was issued on Thursday to sell 25,000 tonnes of one percent sulphur straight-run material, loading between February 25-27. The tender closes next week.

A Tunisian tender was due to be awarded on Friday. The tender requires a 40,000 tonne high sulphur cracked cargo to arrive between Feb 18 and 20, and be exchanged for a 40,000 tonne Tunisian low sulphur straight-run cargo. One dealer said he thought the value of the straight-run portion would be $10 or more over the fob mean of quoted low sulphur quotes fob Tunisia.
A Turkish tender to buy 50,000 tonnes of low sulphur fuel oil closed on Thursday.
Naphtha prices held steady but only due to strength in NWE prices that bucked the sharp selloff in crude futures and blew out the crack spreads.
